nodes.summary: For every natural number $m$ there are natural numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ with $m = \lfloor a^2/8 \rfloor + \lfloor b^2/8 \rfloor + \lfloor c^2/8 \rfloor$.
nodes.title: Sums of three terms of the sequence ⌊n²/8⌋

nodes.summary: Every natural number $n$ that is not of the form $4^a (8b + 7)$ with natural numbers $a, b$ is a sum of three squares: there are natural numbers $x, y, z$ with $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = n$.
nodes.title: Legendre's three-square theorem

nodes.summary: The Hurwitz class number is the function $H$ from the natural numbers to the rationals given by $H(0) = -1/12$; $H(N) = 0$ if $N \equiv 1$ or $2 \pmod 4$; and, for $N > 0$ with $N \equiv 0$ or $3 \pmod 4$, $H(N)$ is the number of equivalence classes of positive-definite integral binary quadratic forms of discriminant $-N$, primitive or not, where the class of a form equivalent to $a (x^2 + y^2)$ for some positive…
nodes.title: Hurwitz class number

nodes.summary: If a natural number $n$ is a sum of three squares of natural numbers, then $n$ is not of the form $4^a (8b + 7)$ with natural numbers $a, b$.
nodes.title: Converse of Legendre's three-square theorem

nodes.title: Legendre-symbol recursion for three-square counts

nodes.summary: For a natural number $m$, let $r_3(m)$ denote the number of ordered triples of integers $(x, y, z)$ with $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = m$. For every positive natural number $n$ divisible by $4$, $r_3(n) = r_3(n/4)$. This is the case $4 \mid n$ of Gauss's formula for $r_3$.
nodes.title: Removing a factor of 4 preserves the three-square count

nodes.summary: For every positive natural number $n$ with $n \equiv 3 \pmod 8$, the number $r_3(n)$ of ordered triples $(x, y, z)$ of integers with $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = n$ equals $24 H(n)$, where $H$ is the Hurwitz class number.
nodes.title: Gauss's three-square formula, residue 3 modulo 8

nodes.summary: For every positive natural number $n$ with $n \equiv 1$, $2$, $5$ or $6 \pmod 8$, the number $r_3(n)$ of ordered triples $(x, y, z)$ of integers with $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = n$ equals $12 H(4n)$, where $H$ is the Hurwitz class number.
nodes.title: Gauss's three-square formula, residues 1, 2, 5, 6 modulo 8

nodes.summary: For a natural number $m$, let $r_3(m)$ denote the number of ordered triples of integers $(x, y, z)$ with $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = m$. For every positive natural number $n$ with $n \equiv 7 \pmod 8$, $r_3(n) = 0$. This is the case $n \equiv 7 \pmod 8$ of Gauss's formula for $r_3$.
nodes.title: Numbers congruent to 7 modulo 8 are not sums of three squares

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $r_3(n)$ is the number of ordered triples $(x, y, z)$ of integers in the interval $[-n, n]$ with $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = n$. Every integer solution of $x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = n$ lies in this interval (also for $n = 0$), so $r_3(n)$ is the number of all ordered integer solutions.
nodes.title: Number of representations as a sum of three squares
